KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry and cool weather through Tuesday night. 
Breezy, especially across Cape Cod and the Islands. 

Anomalous 1030+ mb high pressure over southeast Ontario Monday,
builds eastward into Quebec Tuesday, providing dry and cool 
weather for Southern New England through at least Tue night. 
Northeast gradient will maintain breezy conditions, especially 
across southeast MA, including Cape Cod and Islands. Model 
soundings here support NE winds 15-20 mph with gusts up to 25 
mph at times, less wind away from the coastline. 

Abundant sunshine Monday afternoon, except post frontal strato-
cu over southeast MA from departing frontal wave, combined with 
cool northeast flow over the relatively mild ocean. Mid/high 
clouds will preclude radiational cooling tonight, but a very dry
airmass (dew pts in the 40s and 50s) will be sufficient for min
temps to fall into 40s, except low to mid 50s along the coast, 
including metro Boston, Providence and Hartford.

Tuesday, short wave over the OH valley today spreads mid/high 
clouds into SNE tonight and Tue. However mid level confluent 
flow over the region will provide sufficient subsidence for dry 
weather to prevail. These mid/high clouds will yield filtered 
sunshine Tue. Cooler temps aloft (+7C to +9C) combined with 
subsidence inversion from 1030+ mb high, will yield another day 
of cooler than normal highs Tue, with highs only in the low to 
mid 60s, about 10 degs below normal. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...Monitoring the potential for a strong coastal 
low to form mid to late week, bringing chances for strong winds,
rainfall, and coastal flood/erosion concerns heading into the 
weekend.

Deterministic and ensemble guidance continue to indicate 
potential for a strong coastal low to form Wednesday into the 
later half of the week. While there is still a large amount of 
uncertainty in the guidance, the overarching trend is indicating
the low slowly meanders north into the waters south of 
Nantucket; however, each subsequent model run has trended the 
track further east. The ECMWF ensemble is showing about a 50/50 
member spread on if the low tracks NW of the 40N/70W benchmark 
while the GFS ensemble is much more spread, stretching from the 
DelMarVa coast to Georges Bank, and the Canadian ensemble 
members are majority far east of the benchmark. Regardless, this
system is likely to bring strong winds, rough seas, rain, and 
the potential for erosion/coastal flooding. It is important to 
note that the exact track and strength of the low will strongly 
influence the magnitude of gusts, QPF, and how far inland the 
rain extends.

Highest confidence at this time pertains to winds, especially 
over the waters. As the low deepens and approaches to the south,
the Canadian high over Quebec is also likely to strengthen and 
expand, leading to a tighter pressure gradient over New England.
This will support the development of gusty winds along the 
south coast, Cape/Islands, and the waters by Wednesday 
morning... before the arrival of the low. Confidence continues 
to increase in at least Gale Force winds (34kts/40mph) across 
the southern waters, and a Gale Watch continues for Tuesday 
evening through at least Thursday morning. As the low continues 
to deepen on approach, winds are likely to increase, especially 
across the outer waters. By Friday night/Saturday morning, the 
latest ECMWF ensemble shows widespread 20 to 30 percent 
probabilities of 50 knots (57 mph) across the waters, with a 30 
to 40 percent bullseye over Cape Cod Bay. While the winds over 
land along the south coast, Cape, and Islands throughout the 
week are more likely to be a touch lighter than the marine 
winds, they're still expected to be gusty... more on the order 
of 25-35 mph along the immediate coast.

This prolonged period of gusty northeasterly winds will build 
rough seas and raise the threat for coastal flooding and 
erosion, especially for east facing beaches. Latest coastal 
flooding guidance from the Steven's Institute shows chances for 
Nantucket and Boston nearing/entering Action Stage. Given the 
previously discussed uncertainty in track and strength, 
confidence remains on the lower end for rainfall totals. 
Ensemble guidance has ticked up slightly in totals compared to 
previous runs, with the ECMWF ensemble showing 50 to 70 percent 
probability for 2"+ in 48 hours (20 to 40 percent for 4"+ in 48 
hours) over the Cape and Islands, but the GFS ensemble only 
shows 30 to 50 percent probability (10 percent for 4"+ in 48 
hours).
